title: Admin surface hardening: SAML assertion binding, audit canonicalization, and token scoping refactor
creator: Priya Menon
description: Summary: This ticket consolidates several security review and pen-test findings across the admin surface: unscoped token elevation paths, insufficient SAML assertion binding (replay and session fixation concerns), and gaps in audit logging that make post-incident reconstruction unreliable. Goal: deliver a targeted set of changes that close critical paths, provide tamper-evident admin audit trails, and refactor token scoping so privileged actions require explicit scoped tokens and MFA enforcement. The work is intended to be rolled out in phases behind feature flags and validated with a red-team verification pass.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No open critical/severe findings from the external pen-test targeted at admin flows. 2) Admin CRUD actions emit canonicalized audit events (actor_id, actor_type, resource_id, resource_type, action, pre_image_hash, post_image_hash, sequence_id) with immutability guarantees. 3) SAML assertions are bound to sessions (in-flight replay attacks mitigated) and NameID plus session index are validated against active session store. 4) All privileged API endpoints require explicit scoped admin tokens or elevated session flag; default user tokens cannot perform privileged operations. 5) Rollout feature flag with canary on internal dedicated account and telemetry showing zero regressions in latency for admin APIs.
steps: 1. Implement token scoping: add scope checks to admin middleware and enforce token provenance for all privileged routes. 2. Add MFA enforcement toggle: require elevated sessions to have recent MFA when performing destructive admin actions. 3. Harden SAML processing: verify assertion audience, require session binding via NameID/session-index, and reject reused assertions. 4. Rework audit schema: introduce canonical fields, event chaining (prev_sequence_hash), and write-through to immutable append-only storage with retention policy. 5. Migrate existing audit entries to v2 schema with backfill tooling and validation. 6. Create feature flags and canary rollout pipeline. 7. Run internal regression and red-team tests then coordinate external pen-test re-verification.
test_plan: Unit tests for middleware and scope checks, integration tests for SAML binding and session store behavior, property tests for audit event sequencing, synthetic red-team scenarios reproducing pen-test findings (elevation via unscoped tokens, SAML replay, CSRF on admin console), and an external pen-test re-audit. Monitor dashboards for error spikes and latency during canary. Post-rollout verification: spot-check audit immutability and end-to-end reconstruction of a simulated incident within 30 minutes.
notes: Pen-test findings referenced in report PT-2025-01: elevation-via-unscoped-token, saml-replay, missing-audit-events. Engineering spike (ENG-60210) validated that most admin endpoints are behind a permissive check that lacks token-scope binding. PO asked to avoid changing public API signatures; prefer middleware enforcement where possible. MFA UX discussions to be coordinated with PM and Design (see linked DES ticket).
